title: Blood Compressor — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Blood Compressor's rich face, its first round at Study tier, a proposal: the vessel prototype and the plugin's face gathered where the page imagines them; the plugin's body take beside the three body knobs, and one made walk that tests the sympathetic knob's sentence; the plugin's attack take beside the attack lesson, and one made walk down to the attack knob's floor that tests the page's 'set attack to 0'. Both made pieces run the plugin's own engine, held to it sample for sample. I grow when the Mapping earns a piece that tests its numbers rather than restates them. I never hold the entry's words.

offers.what: The paragraph 'When students set attack=0 and feel the compressor lunge' describes a setting this compressor cannot reach. Measured on the plugin's own engine (attack floor piece and check.mjs): asking for 0 or 1 ms gives the 5 ms floor bit for bit; at the floor, on the drum loop at threshold −36, ratio 10, the vessel moves +0.1 dB in a kick's first 5 ms (it does not close; the 5 ms nerve comes first), then −8.4 dB by 10 ms: the click passes and the boom is clamped. The instant clamp the sentence names needs no floor and no nerve, and then closes −16.9 dB inside the same 5 ms. The 200 ms half holds (−0.2 dB by 10 ms). Suggest the paragraph say what the floor does. If tuning item 2's proposed words are used, drop the crest factor as the evidence: with no floor and no nerve the crest rises too (14.5 to 27.7 dB, against 25.3 at the floor), so a rising crest does not show the nerve; the first 5 ms does.

The Sympathetic activation bullet says the knob 'globally raises threshold + reduces release time, simulating a stressed body that compresses more aggressively'. Measured (the stressed body piece and check.mjs): on the body take's settings, a raised line squeezes less at every step, a quicker release holds less on average, and the two together squeeze less than at rest at every rise from 0 to 12 dB, −1.4 dB average and −5.3 deepest at +12 against −9.2 and −13.2 at rest. The plugin's knob drops the line 12 dB and squeezes more (−15.1, −23.3). Change 'raises threshold' to 'lowers the threshold', or take tuning item 5's proposed words, which already describe the build.

Item 3 (Attack) names one floor, '~5 ms minimum delay', where the build has two: a fixed 5 ms nerve delay before the reflex, and an attack time that cannot go under 5 ms. The check shows both: asking for 0 ms gives the 5 ms attack bit for bit, and from rest the wall first moves 5.17 ms after the hit. Suggest: 'a fixed 5 ms nerve-conduction delay before the reflex, and an attack that cannot be set below 5 ms'.

pieces.title: The vessel, across · Stage 2 prototype v3
pieces.caption: **The cross-section this section describes, built.** One compressor drives both the sound and the picture: a heartbeat (lub, dub, 72 bpm) runs through the vessel, the walls clamp when the pressure crosses the amber systolic line, the baroreceptors light, and the opening follows the gain. Blood cells ride the lumen and squeeze faster through the narrow parts. Drag the line or the slider; it runs with the sound off too, and Sound on starts the heartbeat. Gathered as the steward made it, 2026-10-14. Its knobs are five of the page's six (no sidechain) plus input and makeup, and the beating heart icon the text puts at the bottom is not in it; the heartbeat is the sound source instead.

pieces.title: The plugin's face · inside the vessel, looking downstream
pieces.caption: **The face the plugin got, October 2026.** Not the cross-section above: you are inside the artery looking down it, and each beat rolls away from the glass as a ring of wall. Pink where the wall is pushed past the systolic line, dark bands where the muscle squeezes, a crown of baroreceptors that flares while the reflex fires. The strip on the glass stands in for a host: sound on, then a heartbeat or a drum loop. The editor is VST Template's own, built from the plugin's parameter table (`plugin/ui/build_face.py`); the plugin itself is not yet built. This is the text's last line taken literally: you are looking inside someone's neck.

verdicts.why: A gathered record of the cross-section the section describes; its caption names where the build departs (five of six controls, no sidechain, no heart icon), all checked in the source.
The caption says plainly that this is not the section's cross-section but a view from inside the artery; its one console line, the JUCE placeholder, is expected outside a host.

pieces.title: the body take · the plugin's C++ engine
pieces.caption: **The three body knobs, one at a time, on one drum loop.** Six seconds each: at rest, stressed (sympathetic 1), old (vessel age 1), breathing (heart-rate variability 1). Threshold −30 dB, ratio 4, attack 60 ms, release 300 ms, each section matched to −27 dBFS so you hear the shape, not the level. Average squeeze, deepest: at rest −9.2, −13.3 dB; stressed −15.2, −23.4; old −10.7, −15.5; breathing −9.3, −14.7, with the squeeze swinging 2.5 dB beat to beat against 0.3 at rest (`plugin/out/body-take.json`). Rendered 2026-10-24 by `plugin/check/render_body.py`. Nobody has listened to it yet, the scroll says.

pieces.file: Blood Compressor — rich — the stressed body.html
pieces.title: The stressed body · raise the line, or drop it?
pieces.caption:
**The sympathetic bullet says a stressed body raises the threshold and compresses more aggressively. Can it do both?** Four steps on the plugin's own engine (held to it sample for sample) and a drum loop made from sine and noise: the body at rest; the systolic line alone, where higher squeezes less at every step; the smooth muscle alone, where a quicker release holds less on average; and last the stressed body two ways, answered before heard. As written, line raised and muscle four times quicker, it squeezes less than at rest at every rise from 0 to 12 dB: −1.4 dB on average at +12 against −9.2 at rest. As the plugin built it, line dropped 12 dB, it squeezes more: −15.1. Loudness is matched. The page sizes neither move; the four-times release and the 12 dB are the plugin's.

as built: T′ = T − 12·S, attack′ = attack ⁄ (1 + S), release′ = release ⁄ (1 + 3·S)

(the stressed line) = (the line at rest) − 12 dB × (how stressed, 0 to 1); the reflex up to twice as quick, the muscle up to four times

verdicts.why: Caption numbers match plugin/out/body-take.json row for row and settings match render_body.py; byte-identical to the steward's render. Unheard, and the caption says so.

verdicts.file: Blood Compressor — rich — the stressed body.html
verdicts.why: A test that comes out against the text: as written it squeezes less than rest at every rise (−1.4 at +12 vs −9.2), recomputed on the plugin's file; faithful, since it names the amounts as the plugin's; walks up from rest, to the line alone, to the muscle alone, to the test. The crest reading of 'aggressive' agrees (17.1 written, 20.0 rest, 24.6 built).

pieces.title: the attack lesson · the plugin's C++ engine
pieces.caption: **The lesson as the plugin's engine renders it.** A drum loop, 4.8 s per section: as it arrives; attack at its floor, 5 ms; attack 80 ms; attack 80 ms with a 40 ms release, the vessel breathing with the beat. Threshold −36 dB, ratio 10, each section matched to −27 dBFS. Rendered 2026-10-24 by `plugin/check/render_take.py`, whose notes say the floor clamps the kick's front; the piece beside this measures that it doesn't. Nobody has listened to it yet, the scroll says.

pieces.title: Set attack to zero · a walk down to the knob's floor
pieces.caption:
**Can this compressor lunge?** Four steps on the plugin's own engine, held to it sample for sample, and a drum loop made from sine and noise: one kick alone in the vessel; the body noticing and acting at 200 ms, baroreceptors lit and the nerve's 5 ms marked; the attack swept down until the knob stops at 5 ms; and the sentence tested, answered before heard. Asking the engine for 0 ms gives the 5 ms floor bit for bit. At the floor the vessel does not close at all in a kick's first 5 ms (+0.1 dB, still letting go of the last hit), then clamps, −8.4 dB by 10 ms: a click, then a flattened boom. The instant clamp the sentence describes takes no floor and no nerve, which this compressor refuses; that body closes −16.9 dB inside the same 5 ms. The crest rises in both, 14.5 dB to 25.3 and 27.7, so crest can't tell them apart. Loudness is matched; whether the floor sounds like a lunge is for your ear.

g[n] = c·g[n−1] + (1 − c)·target[n − d],  c = e^(−1 ⁄ (fs·τ)),  τ = max(5 ms, attack),  d = 5 ms · fs

(squeeze now) = c × (squeeze a sample ago) + (1 − c) × (what the line asked for 5 ms ago); the reflex never goes under 5 ms, and the nerve's 5 ms sits before it at every setting

verdicts.why: Byte-identical to the steward's render; the caption's claim about render_take.py is true (its docstring lines 7–8 contradict lines 16–17 and the engine). That should be filed as an offer with section → bundle, which the challenger may not write.

A test the build fails as the sentence says it should not: at the floor +0.12 dB in a kick's first 5 ms, −8.38 by 10 ms, against −16.85 with no floor and no nerve, recomputed on the plugin's file. Walks up in four steps. Taste notes: a 'floor off, nerve kept' take would show the nerve alone holds the first 5 ms (+0.13), and step 3's 'the DSP section says so too' blurs the two floors.
